title: ECB already had large support for rate hike in October, accounts show
Nam Lee Pressed Metal Industries earnings rise 28.8% y-o-y to $32 mil
article:
For FY2026 ended Sept 30, Nam Lee Pressed Metal Industries has reported net profit of $32 million, up 28.8% y-o-y. Revenue jumped 38.3% y-o-y to $288.6 million. A final dividend of two cents (down one cent from FY2025), has been declared.

Gross profit rose 28.5% y-o-y to $65.6 million while overall operating expenses climbed 26.7% y-o-y to $24.5 million. Overall, the Mainboard-listed company performed more strongly in the second-half of its financial year.

On a segmental basis, the aluminium segment showed the strongest improvement, with revenue leaping 58.3% y-o-y to $213.4 million. Revenue for the steel segment was up 42.2% y-o-y to $54.2 million. However, segment revenue for UPVC products weakened, dropping by 41.4% y-o-y to $20.9 million.

The company held cash and fixed deposits of nearly $33.9 million, with borrowings of $19.6 million. Operating cash flow decreased to $20.2 million due to an increase in inventories and receivables of $10.3 million and $28.7 million respectively, compared to the previous corresponding period of a $0.3 million decrease in inventories and receivables increase of $13.7 million.

The company sees a stable outlook on both industrial and construction sub segments and expects FY2027’s revenue to remain broadly in line with the current financial year. It cautions about the impact of inflation, higher interest rates, logistics and imported raw materials, adding that it will remain focused on prudent capital and resource management.

Shares in Nam Lee closed unchanged on Nov 26 at 53 cents.
